analysis:
Compared the complete supplied BASE/HEAD ClusterSetupLinkExchange.swift and its patch. HEAD lines 113–125 add an immutable, Equatable pairing identity containing public pins, cluster ID, link epoch and edge ID; lines 170–184 expose the identity used to construct a responder. Neither secret bytes nor the secret-file path enter this identity. Existing key derivation/domain separation (136–157), interface-bound listener configuration (181–187), body bounds and peer-member validation remain unchanged. These additions alone establish no authorization, encryption, disclosure or availability regression against A-001, TB-003, TB-007, T-053 or T-058.
Examined docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md:456–664; only 581–588 change, documenting automatic pairing refresh and a restart fallback. Surrounding tenant isolation, encrypted cache, precision, update and purge claims are unchanged; no new T-041 regression is evidenced.
ClusterService.swift is supplied only as metadata plus a truncated orientation patch. It introduces listener-check state and a Listening dependency, but does not expose the refresh implementation. Integration must inspect its HEAD 337–420 and related listener lifecycle changes: ensure pairing replacement/removal retires both exchange and control listeners, queued old-peer commands cannot cross into new pairing authority, and refresh failure does not retain obsolete authority or cause restart churn. Verify the epoch-change contract underlying identity comparison, and reconcile documentation's 'within seconds' claim with actual refresh behavior. These are unresolved PR-specific contracts, not demonstrated missing controls. No serving-grant, billing, fan-helper or installer behavior changes are shown in the reviewed executable source; this is a local review, not clearance of missing service implementation.
